fields.description:
## Context / Problem
The workflow editor currently presents authored YAML/BPMN configuration without a trustworthy view of the effective criteria policy derived from built-ins plus project overlays. RP-06 adds an immutable derived policy and an explicit project applicability rule; exposing derived state as if it were editable topology would create a second policy authority and make misconfiguration difficult to diagnose.

## Approach
Extend the workflow-editor server to obtain the S1 `CriteriaSnapshot` for the selected repository and expose a narrow, read-only Effective Policy view. Keep Authored Workflow as the only editable YAML/BPMN topology. The effective view shows snapshot digest/source, criterion id, gate, execution tier, effective posture/threshold, applicability summary, enabled/disabled state, and a concise derived reason. It never serializes edits back into workflow or project routing.

At authoring/save validation, a new `project.*` code-review LLM criterion must have a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative `applies_to` globs. The editor rejects an empty/missing selector with the exact `["**"]` repository-wide remedy. Built-in entries, project DET criteria, and plan-review criteria retain their distinct trigger authoring controls and are not forced through this field.

Keep stored execution trace and per-call debugging detail out of the editor response. The Effective Policy panel is configuration provenance, not a review-result/status viewer. Repository or validation errors fail the save or mark the effective view unavailable with a located, actionable message; they do not silently display packaged defaults as effective policy.

## Rationale and Compatibility
A read-only projection makes the centralized pattern visible while preserving one authored source of topology. Older workflow files remain readable. The UI and server add fields without rewriting saved YAML/BPMN, and rollback removes the panel/endpoint while leaving authored artifacts unchanged.

## Testing
Use server contract tests with real overlay/snapshot compilation and focused editor DOM/state tests. The oracle is the serialized authored document remaining byte-equivalent while the read-only view changes with project policy. Negative controls cover built-in empty trigger semantics, project DET, and plan review. Error fixtures prove unavailable policy is explicit and save validation is fail-loud.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The editor renders distinct Authored Workflow and read-only Effective Policy sections, and no action in the effective section mutates or serializes YAML/BPMN.
- [x] Effective Policy data comes from the repository-bound `CriteriaSnapshot` and displays digest/source plus concise criterion gate, tier, posture, applicability, and enabled/disabled provenance.
- [x] Creating or saving a project code-review LLM criterion with missing, empty, non-list, or blank globs is refused with the criterion location and `use ["**"] for repository-wide` remedy.
- [x] Built-in secondary triggers, project DET selector controls, and plan-review `applies_at`/`trigger` authoring remain valid negative controls and are not subjected to the project-LLM glob rule.
- [x] A snapshot load/validation failure marks Effective Policy unavailable with an actionable located error and never substitutes packaged defaults or permits an invalid save.
- [x] Server and editor tests prove policy changes update only the derived view while authored workflow round-trips byte-equivalently.
- [x] Editor payloads contain no per-unit discovery trace, raw prompt/context body, provider response, or secret.
